text:
In general, yes submitting counts as starting a process and there is a prohibition on parallel visa applications. However the affect of this is reduced by two things. 

(1) PIBA should keep you on the same student visa while they process your partner-visa application (you can read about this here https://aic.org.il/applying-for-partner-visa-while-having-another-visa/). 

(2) Occasionally, PIBA is annoying and will try to "downgrade" applicants from a student visa to a tourist visa. But even if this happens there is no apparent legal prohibition against studying while on a tourist visa, and as a result we understand that universities and institutions are mainly concerned that their students have a legal status in Israel, and so will not cause problems for students who are placed on a tourist visa while having their partner-visa application decided. You should try and confirm this yourself with your university (explain that you are here on a student visa, you are applying for a partner visa etc). But in short, this should not be a reason to hold you back from submitting your application.
